briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 2, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Heatwaves and the Spread of Climate Disasters
sections.content: The global community is experiencing a 'cruel summer,' groaning under disasters caused by extreme heatwaves and droughts [1, 4, 6]. Domestically, a record-breaking heatwave reaching 42.5 degrees Celsius has swept across the nation, including Yangsan, Gyeongnam, leading to a surge in heat-related illnesses and even fatalities [11, 33, 34, 38]. Europe is also suffering from large-scale wildfires and severe droughts [7, 8], while in the Jeju region, climate disasters are widely spreading, with heatwaves, droughts, and high water temperatures occurring simultaneously, putting carrot farms in a state of emergency [13, 35, 36]. Scientists are detecting this rapid acceleration of global warming [41], warning that climate change is no longer a distant threat [40, 51]. In this situation, a thorough review is necessary to ensure there are no blind spots in heatwave safety measures [10, 37].

sections.title: ⚠️ Increasing Threats to Ecosystems and the Economy
sections.content: Ongoing climate change poses a direct threat to ecosystems. The case of the 'Hongjul butterfly,' designated as an endangered wild species in August, illustrates the reality that climate change threatens survival [2]. In the economic sector, the impact is severe, with the global wine industry facing existential threats such as changes in grape varieties and reduced production due to climate change [3]. Domestically, late monsoon rains and unprecedented heatwaves are significantly impacting daily life, making menu changes and supply chain restructuring unavoidable for the catering industry [12]. These multifaceted threats suggest that climate change can destabilize overall societal stability, extending beyond mere environmental issues.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts Towards a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Positive movements to address climate change are also actively being observed. Hyundai Engineering & Construction has unveiled its ESG response strategies for safety, quality, and climate change [5], and Samsung SDI is accelerating its RE100 efforts by expanding eco-friendly power [30]. Local governments are exploring the transition to carbon-neutral cities through the Pohang World Green Growth Forum [14], and Cheongju City is carrying out environmental cleanup and carbon-neutral campaigns, demonstrating continued local-level actions [16]. Notably, Dongducheon City stands out for its efforts towards a circular economy, including signing agreements for waste banner upcycling and carbon-neutral practices [15, 17]. In the transportation sector, Chungju City's expanded operation of hydrogen buses [20] and the promotion of electric delivery motorcycles [18] are considered important steps in accelerating the transition to a carbon-neutral city. Internationally, corporate-level global cooperation is also active, with Korea Zinc proposing integrated cooperation with Chile on critical minerals and green energy, seeking 'carbon-neutral partners' [21, 32].

sections.title: 📰 Renewable Energy Expansion and Current Challenges
sections.content: Efforts towards renewable energy transition are continuing. Hanmi Group has introduced direct power purchase agreements for renewable energy, laying the groundwork for companies to achieve RE100 [22], and in Finland, the world's largest 'sand battery' has begun operation, representing an innovative attempt to address the intermittency of renewable energy [23]. Domestically, the Speaker of the National Assembly visited the Jeju Hallim Offshore Wind Farm, praising it as an exemplary model and discussing support for clean energy, thus emphasizing the importance of offshore wind power generation [24, 26, 28]. However, challenges still exist in the process of renewable energy expansion. With solar power generation experiencing output curtailment roughly one day out of three, the establishment of energy storage systems (ESS) to accommodate this is still insufficient [27]. Furthermore, market volatility is observed, with solar and new renewable energy-related ETFs recording declines in the 10% range [29], indicating that sustained policy and technical support will be necessary for a stable energy transition.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Voice on Climate Response
sections.content: In the international community, warning voices about the severity of climate change are growing louder. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez directly stated that 'climate change kills,' referring to the large-scale wildfires in his country, sounding an alarm for climate change deniers [40, 51]. Minnesota's harsh July temperatures numerically demonstrate the responsibility of climate change, emphasizing its impact in various regions [46]. However, news that an international climate change tracking project is facing difficulties [47] suggests challenges in global cooperation and implementation for responding to the climate crisis. In this situation, efforts to find 'reasons for hope in the face of climate change' [43] and climate change responses through agroecology [48], among other diverse perspectives and solution-seeking, must accompany these challenges.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has simultaneously illuminated the global threats posed by climate change and the diverse domestic and international efforts to overcome them. Our sustained attention and practical actions to overcome the climate crisis are more crucial than ever. This concludes today's climate briefing.
